comment: Source texts for the ASR eval corpus. `text` may contain [[slnc N]] Apple Speech Synthesis pause commands; they are stripped from the reference transcript. `hard_terms` are the vocabulary items the recognizer must reproduce; their union doubles as the simulated user dictionary for vocabulary biasing. Numeric content is authored in digit/symbol form so the scorer only ever normalizes hypothesis number-words toward the reference, never the reverse.

Good morning team, here is the plan for the week. Olanrewaju wants the release candidate ready by Thursday, which means the remaining bugs need owners today. [[slnc 900]] The crash on resume is the highest priority because it blocks the beta testers. After that comes the memory regression in the history view, which only shows up after about an hour of use. [[slnc 900]] Orttaai should feel faster at the end of this cycle, not slower, so please run the profiler before and after every change. If anything looks risky, flag it in the channel first and we will decide together.

Let me explain how the conditioning work is supposed to land. WhisperKit accepts a promptTokens array inside DecodingOptions, and whatever we pass there becomes the previous context for the decoder. [[slnc 900]] The catch is that the prompt is trimmed to half the token window, so we cannot just dump the whole session transcript into it. We keep the most recent sentences, cap the budget, and drop the prompt entirely whenever the previous decode looked suspicious. [[slnc 900]] That last guard matters because a bad prompt can push the model into a repetition loop, and a repetition loop in a dictation app is far worse than a missing word.

Thanks everyone for joining the retrospective. Overall the launch went smoothly, but there are three things we should do better next time. [[slnc 900]] First, the support documentation went live two days after the feature, which left the help desk answering the same question over and over. Second, we never agreed on who owns the status page, so updates during the incident were slow. [[slnc 900]] Third, and this is the big one, we shipped on a Friday. Nobody wants to debug a payment issue at nine in the evening before a weekend. Let's write these down and actually read them before the next release.

Here is the incident summary for the outage on Tuesday. At around 2:15 pm the PostgreSQL primary ran out of connections because a batch job leaked them for over an hour. [[slnc 900]] The Kubernetes autoscaler then made things worse by doubling the number of workers, each of which opened its own pool. Latency climbed past eight seconds and checkout effectively stopped. [[slnc 900]] We recovered by killing the batch job and cycling the connection pooler, and the whole event lasted 34 minutes. The follow up items are a connection budget per service and an alert on pool saturation, both assigned and due next sprint.

[[slnc 900]] The agenda is deliberately light, one morning of planning, one afternoon of open discussion, and the rest is unstructured time to actually talk to each other. Last year we packed the schedule so tight that people left more tired than when they arrived. [[slnc 900]] Please fill in the dietary form by the end of the month, and if you need a visa letter, ask early because the embassy has been slow lately.

I want to dictate some thoughts about the book before I forget them. The first half is a fairly conventional memoir, childhood, school, the move to the city, but the voice is so dry and funny that none of it drags. [[slnc 900]] Then the middle section switches to the mother's letters and the whole thing opens up. You suddenly understand that every story in the first half was secondhand, and the letters quietly correct the record. [[slnc 900]] The ending felt rushed to me, maybe twenty pages where it needed sixty, but I still think it is the best thing she has written.

Here is my honest review of the trip for the travel blog. The old town is genuinely beautiful, narrow streets, tiled courtyards, and the kind of bakeries that make you plan your day around bread. [[slnc 900]] The catch is the crowds. By ten in the morning the main square is shoulder to shoulder, and the famous viewpoint has a queue like an airport. Go at sunrise or do not go at all. [[slnc 900]] Food was cheaper than I expected, dinner for two came to about 40 euros with wine, and the seafood place by the harbor deserves every bit of its reputation.

Release checklist walkthrough, please follow along. First, Oyinbooke signs the build and the notarization ticket gets stapled before anything is uploaded. [[slnc 900]] Second, the appcast entry is generated with the new version number and the release notes, and Sparkle picks it up from the same feed we have always used. Do not hand edit the XML, the script exists for a reason. [[slnc 900]] Third, we watch the crash dashboard for two hours after the rollout. If anything spikes we pull the appcast entry, which stops new updates without affecting anyone who already installed.

The two plants with the curled leaves go in the bin, not the compost, just to be safe. [[slnc 900]] Garlic goes in before the first frost, pointy end up, about a hand's width apart. Last year we planted too shallow and half of it heaved out of the ground by February. [[slnc 900]] The roses get one last feed, then nothing until spring. And please label the beds this time, because by March nobody remembers what is where.

[[slnc 900]] The npm workspace split also landed, so the design system builds independently and the main app no longer rebuilds the world on every change. Local build times dropped from four minutes to about 90 seconds. [[slnc 900]] Remaining work is the settings pages and the test utilities, both scheduled for the next two sprints.

Here is the local model setup I recommend for the polish stage. Install Ollama for the daily driver because it starts fast and stays out of the way, and keep LM Studio around for experiments where you want to watch the token stream. [[slnc 900]] The Qwen models are the sweet spot right now, the small one handles punctuation cleanup easily and fits in memory next to the transcription model. [[slnc 900]] Whatever you pick, pin the exact version in the settings and write it in the runbook, because silent model upgrades have burned us twice already this quarter.

[[slnc 900]] On the product side, Oluwaseun's team shipped the payment integration rewrite and the failed charge rate dropped by a third in the first week. [[slnc 900]] Hiring remains the bottleneck. Recording my practice talk, feedback welcome. The talk opens with a story about the first outage I ever caused, which gets a laugh and buys me goodwill for the dry middle section. [[slnc 900]] The middle is three lessons about on call culture, each with one chart and one concrete change we made. I am worried the second lesson runs long, if you see people checking phones, that is where. [[slnc 900]] The ending circles back to the outage story with the fix we eventually shipped, and lands on the line, the system is allowed to fail, the team is not. Total time should be 18 minutes.

Architecture note for the new contributor, welcome aboard. Persistence goes through GRDB and every table has a record struct next to it, please do not write raw SQL in view code, there is a manager for that. [[slnc 900]] The transcription side is an actor, and the one invariant you must never break is that committedSampleCount only moves forward during a live session. Everything else, the clips, the speculative tail, the merge, hangs off that number. [[slnc 900]] Read the tests before the implementation, they are shorter and they tell you what the code promises rather than how it keeps the promise.

Code review notes on the checkout branch. The useEffectCallback wrapper is doing too much, it fetches, it subscribes, and it writes analytics, and every one of those deserves its own effect with its own dependency list. [[slnc 900]] Naming is drifting again, half the new helpers are in camelCase and the other half in snake case copied from the backend client. Pick one, the linter config is already in the repo. [[slnc 900]] The state machine for the payment steps is genuinely nice work though, the impossible states are actually impossible now, and the tests read like documentation. Approve with comments.

Debug diary for the silence bug. A user reported that Orttaai swallowed the first word whenever they started speaking immediately after the hotkey. [[slnc 900]] The trail led to the noSpeechThreshold interacting badly with the EnergyVAD framing, the first hundred milliseconds were being classified as silence and the decoder skipped the opening token. [[slnc 900]] The fix pads the detected speech region on both sides instead of trusting the raw frame boundary, and the regression test synthesizes exactly this case, a word starting within the first frame. Shipped in the patch release, and the user confirmed the fix the same evening.
